name: TX-06
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent Jake Ellzey holds an overwhelming cash advantage: $2.65 million on hand versus about $13,600 for Danny Minton
The district leans roughly 11 points Republican, anchoring the race to the GOP
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 3 percent
No polls, no expert ratings, and no outside spending signal a competitive race
model.rationale: Ellzey's incumbency, massive fundraising edge, and the district's eleven-point Republican lean give him a clear advantage, and prediction markets price a Democratic upset near three percent. With no polls showing competition and no outside money targeting the seat, the fundamentals point to a comfortable but not untouchable Republican hold.
model.watch: Any independent polling showing a single-digit race or significant outside spending against Ellzey would warrant revisiting the forecast.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican incumbent Jake Ellzey is favored in a North Texas district that has leaned about eleven points Republican. No public general-election polling or expert ratings cover the race, so the picture rests on fundamentals. Ellzey combines incumbency with a dominant financial position, reporting roughly $2.65 million on hand after raising more than $5.4 million for the cycle.

Democrat Danny Minton has raised about $44,000 and holds under $14,000 in the bank, with no reported outside support or opposition spending on either side. Prediction markets give Democrats only about a three percent chance of an upset. With no evidence of a competitive dynamic emerging, the seat looks firmly in Republican hands, though the absence of polling leaves some uncertainty about the exact size of the expected margin.
